summary: Added an opt-in admin hot-reload API that drains inference, reloads selected loaded pure-Python SGLang modules across scheduler workers, rebinds existing classes and direct imports, recaptures decode graphs, and preserves model weights.

tests.what_was_measured: Five compatibility, regression, and adversarial tests: live class rebinding after an edited source file, direct-import rebinding, rejection of non-SGLang/unloaded/native modules, and graph-recapture dispatch without a weight-loading call.

tests.command: pre-commit run --files <all changed source, test, and documentation files>
tests.what_was_measured: Repository formatting, import order, Ruff, codespell, syntax, and policy hooks.

tests.command: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m sglang.launch_server <tiny-random-llama> --attention-backend triton --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 2 --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 --enable-dev-reload --admin-api-key dev-secret; POST /generate; POST /dev/reload; POST /generate
tests.what_was_measured: Real MI350X/gfx950 engine execution, HTTP auth and validation, in-process module reload, decode graph recapture (0.48 s), absence of another weight-load phase, and identical eight-token greedy output before/after reload.
Independent Hugging Face CPU reference exactly matched SGLang output IDs [12, 100, 124, 43, 124, 43, 124, 51].

gpu_execution_evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950; startup graph capture 7.72 s; reload graph recapture 0.48 s; pre/post generation HTTP 200 with identical tokens; GPU returned to 0% use and 0% allocated VRAM after shutdown.
remaining_limitations: No native C++/CUDA/FlyDSL source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
GPU validation covered single-node TP=1 only; multi-rank broadcast was not hardware-tested.
Native extensions, newly imported modules, object-layout changes, process-topology changes, torch.compile artifacts, and JIT kernel changes require restart.
Reload is not transactional when changed module top-level execution fails.
The alternative fault-tolerant scheduler exception loop is not implemented.
The synthetic tiny Llama fixture validates transport and engine execution only, not large-model timing, other architectures, distributed execution, or semantic model quality.
The interactive server transcript was not captured in full; request/response payloads and an explicitly labeled relevant log excerpt are retained.
